chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: The MCA offer that Hayes's band declined
summary: An MCA man offered booking at low pay until the name grew; several members refused, though Lovett and Goodwin would have gone.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: MCA Corporation of America?

Yeah, came here to hear us. They'd heard us. They explained to the band manager, which was Harlan Thomas Leonard at this time, had gone out of music. He had quit music completely. They came here and he told us what he could pay, you know, he said, 'You've got a wonderful band, you've got a good band but you don't have a name' and he said, 'Now, I can pay you according to the name you've got' and he told us what he could pay us.
But as the name improved the salary would improve?
That's right. He said it would take about six months before he could start paying us.
And he wanted you to go out on the road for MCA --
Right.
-- at a certain salary?
Well, several of the fellows, I don't like to call names --
Well, we don't need that.
-- well they turned it down because they figured they were --
They could do better here.
-- worth more than this.
Worth more than that and they could probably make more playing in Kansas City?

Well they could, yes but they didn't realize that during the time we were taking this beating, we had taken a beating for four or five years anyway, so they didn't realize at the time, well we take this further little beating and we've got somebody in front of us now who will try to make us; which we didn't have before. We only had a leader trying to book the band and play in the band and operate the band all at the same time, which is a tremendous job to
do. It's not a one-man operation.
It sure isn't as we all know.
You can't -- you're doing three men's jobs if you try to book the band and see that the band -- take care of all the band business and then play in the band, well see you're doing a three-man job.

Yeah, well that's what Baby and I are doing right now. Baby, what was your feeling when MCA approached the Thoman Hayes band, which then had Harlan Leonard as a leader? Were you ready to go out on the road for MCA?
Oh yeah, sure.
You were?
Oh yeah, yeah.
I was too.
Sure, it wasn't doing anything amounting to anything you know. We needed some money I think at that point.
It was a big chance you had?
Oh yeah.
It was the biggest and best agency in the business?
Oh sure, it was great. I hated to miss that, I'll tell you.
